posts.name: aramis
posts.cooked:
PlatinumWarlock:

That’s nice; I know lots of people with printers.  Regardless of whether you do or not, the pad represents a charge for something that’s effectively being given away of free.  If it’s something you want to pay for, more power to you.  I just think it seems like adding the pads to the GM Kit adds a degree of cost on GtG’s end for something that they’re simultaneously providing for free.

Also, you can drop the subtle accusations of “stealing resources” from my employer; that’s an assumption you’re making all your own, quite incorrectly.

But they are NOT given away for free. The pad is 100 sheets of tangible. Running 100 sheets of tangible at my local UPS store is going to be about 25¢ per side for color on letter, or $0.50 per sheet, so $50. Might be able to get that down to $30 or so by using other sources, or submitting it for bulk printing. That said, if I’m wanting to fill in the data and print, the pad is of no use. If one is wanting blanks, for handwriting, the GM kit is a save over one-offs over time.

SOMEONE is paying for the ink and paper.

My cost for a roughly 4000 page cartrige on my B&W printer is $70 (brother).  About 1.7¢ per side. Plus the paper $5 for 500 sheets. 1¢ per sheet. So, about 4.4¢ per sheet, B&W.

Color inkjets are about $30 per cart, with about 1000 pages per cart, and 4 carts needed (CMYK) So $120 per 1000 pp… 12¢ per side, plus 1¢ for the page, or 25¢ per 2-sided sheet. Hmm… not so cheap. (ink sourced is XL carts for HP cart 950 & 951)

And those costs are before amortization of the printer itself. 

So, understand, if you’re using the printer at work, you’re stealing up to a quarter dollar per sheet, or, alternatively, you need to declare it as taxable perquisates. (in which case, it may still be theft, if they didn’t authorize it, but at least you aren’t cheating on your taxes. Remember, Al Capone was incarcerated not for the crimes, but for not paying taxes on the proceeds…)
